question.problem: Write $\frac{{x}^{2}+10}{{x}^{2}+x}$ in the form $a+\frac{bx+c}{{x}^{2}+x},$ where $a\ne 0.$ What is the value of $a+b+c?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we add and subtract $x$ in the numerator. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+10}{{x}^{2}+x}=\frac{{x}^{2}+x-x+10}{{x}^{2}+x}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}+x-x+10}{{x}^{2}+x} & =\frac{{x}^{2}+x}{{x}^{2}+x}+\frac{-x+10}{{x}^{2}+x} \\  & =1+\frac{-x+10}{{x}^{2}+x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have $a=1,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=10,$ and we get

$$
a+b+c=1+(-1)+10=10.
$$
